Package com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.gametest

Class SkullEyeGameTestsLogic

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.gametest.SkullEyeGameTestsLogic
public final class SkullEyeGameTestsLogic extends Object
Googly eyes on placed mob heads: applying and harvesting them through EyeItemService.useOnSkull(net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player, net.minecraft.world.level.Level, net.minecraft.world.InteractionHand, net.minecraft.world.phys.BlockHitResult), an eyed mob's own head inheriting its eyes (EyeItemService.markHeadDrop(net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity, net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack), reached through each loader's death-drop hook), breaking and re-placing a head, and saving one. The loader adapters' protection-mod ordering around the use call stays source-verified, as for mobs; the rendered eyes and their client-side expressions need a client.

The Heads mod's heads are recognized by block id alone. Tests of the mapping run on every loader, with or without that mod; those placing its heads need it loaded, as it is in Forge development runs, and Forge alone wraps them.

For the in-game steps below, get Optometrist shears as described in EyeItemServiceGameTestsLogic.

  • Method Details

    • brokenHeadKeepsItsEyes

      public static void brokenHeadKeepsItsEyes(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper, net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player player)
      Breaking an eyed head drops a head item carrying its eyes, and placing that item restores them. In game: give a skeleton skull purple eyes, break it in survival, and hover the dropped skull; its tooltip lists googly eyes and the iris color. Place it again; it shows the same purple eyes in the same arrangement.

    • deniedItemUseLeavesHeadsUntouched

      public static void deniedItemUseLeavesHeadsUntouched(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper, net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player player, BiConsumer<net.minecraft.world.phys.BlockHitResult,Boolean> interact)
      A native item-use denial prevents both applying and harvesting head eyes, without consuming the item, damaging shears, or spawning a drop. In game: deny item use on a placed skull with a protection listener while leaving the event uncanceled, then try a Slimy Eye and Optometrist shears.

    • eyedMobDropsAnEyedHead

      public static void eyedMobDropsAnEyedHead(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      An eyed mob's head inherits the mob's eyes; an eyeless mob's head doesn't. In game: give a skeleton purple eyes with /sg admin eyes true and /sg admin tint iris 0.6 0.1 0.8, then let a charged creeper blow it up; its dropped skull lists googly eyes and the iris color, and placed it shows the skeleton's purple eyes. A plain skeleton killed the same way drops a plain skull.

      TODO: this test fails on both loaders for reasons not yet understood, though the behavior works in game; its loader wrappers are commented out until the cause is found.

    • eyedMobsHeadsModHeadInheritsItsEyes

      public static void eyedMobsHeadsModHeadInheritsItsEyes(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      An eyed mob's own Heads-mod head inherits the mob's eyes; another mob's head doesn't. Needs the Heads mod. In game, with Heads installed: give a cow purple eyes with /sg admin eyes true and /sg admin tint iris 0.6 0.1 0.8, raise Heads' cow drop rate to 1 in its config, and kill the cow; its dropped cow head lists googly eyes and the iris color.

    • headEyesSurviveSaveLoad

      public static void headEyesSurviveSaveLoad(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      A head's eyes survive saving and loading its block entity. In game: give a placed skeleton skull purple eyes, leave and rejoin the world; the eyes are still there.

    • headsModBlocksMapToTheirMobs

      public static void headsModBlocksMapToTheirMobs(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      The Heads mod's floor and wall heads map to their mobs by block id, and only its namespace counts. Runs with or without that mod. In game, with Heads installed: sneak with a Googly Eye at a placed Heads cow head, then at a wall-mounted one; both report that they can have eyes. A Heads squid head reports no configuration.

    • headsModHeadTakesKeepsAndGivesUpEyes

      public static void headsModHeadTakesKeepsAndGivesUpEyes(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper, net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player player)
      A Heads-mod head takes a Slimy Eye, keeps its eyes when broken and re-placed, and gives them up to Optometrist shears, as a vanilla head does. Needs the Heads mod. In game, with Heads installed: place a Heads cow head and repeat slimyEyeGivesAPlacedHeadEyes(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper, net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player), brokenHeadKeepsItsEyes(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper, net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player), and optometristHarvestsAPlacedHead(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper, net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player) on it, checking eye state with /data get block where the eyes aren't drawn yet.

    • headsModMobsHaveHeadEyes

      public static void headsModMobsHaveHeadEyes(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Every Heads-mod head with a mob can have eyes, and whatever its roll, it shows the eyes of one of its mob's variants with eyes on the part the head reproduces, though that mob has variants with eyes only elsewhere (a cow's on its body). Runs with or without that mod. In game, with Heads installed: apply Slimy Eyes to several Heads cow heads; once rendering is in, every one shows eyes on its face.

    • optometristHarvestsAPlacedHead

      public static void optometristHarvestsAPlacedHead(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper, net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player player)
      Optometrist shears take a head's eyes off as one Googly Eye; plain shears leave them. In game: give a skeleton skull purple eyes with a Slimy Eye, right-click it with plain shears (nothing happens), then with Optometrist shears; the eyes vanish, a purple Googly Eye pops out, the shearing sound plays, and the shears lose one durability.

    • slimyEyeGivesAPlacedHeadEyes

      public static void slimyEyeGivesAPlacedHeadEyes(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper, net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player player)
      A Slimy Eye gives an eyeless placed head eyes carrying its appearance; an eyed head refuses another. In game: dye a Googly Eye purple, craft it into a Slimy Eye, place a skeleton skull, and right-click the skull with it in survival; the skull gains purple googly eyes, a squelch plays, and the Slimy Eye is used up. Right-click the same skull with a second Slimy Eye; nothing happens and it is kept.

    • slimyEyeRefusesUnconfiguredHeadsAndTheSwitch

      public static void slimyEyeRefusesUnconfiguredHeadsAndTheSwitch(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper, net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player player)
      A head without a definition, or any head while the switch is off, refuses a Slimy Eye. In game: right-click a placed dragon head with a Slimy Eye; nothing happens and the Slimy Eye is kept. Set googlyEyesEnabled = false and right-click a skeleton skull; nothing happens either.
